mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2% indicates accommodative monetary policy, which compresses discount rates for equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active and the rate being below 2% is the condition for positive returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 2%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A one-month rise in unemployment rate above 6.5% signals labor market deterioration, triggering a flight to quality and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors seek safer assets.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE > 6.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and residential sales (RSAFS) signals a contraction in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown. This leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in potential monetary policy easing.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 105 for two consecutive months), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates central bank intervention to prevent a recession.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO < 105 for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates strong economic expansion, which supports equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active and the direction is positive when GDP growth is strong.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 is above its 3-year average, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year inflation rate above 2.5% (CPIAUCSL) signals an inflation shock that triggers a market reaction leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate monetary policy tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY change > 2.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in private employment (PAYEMS) and rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening labor market and monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in recession risk.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS declines and FEDFUNDS rises, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) and low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 2%), the market faces stagflation risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors flee equities for bonds and cash.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS < 2%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.
